history: always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (20 stable releases, linear scan under match.json, no invalid probes; 5 prereleases skipped by policy, 1 tag with no usable asset). One defect, three presentations: silent 0xC0000005 on v1.4.1907/v1.5.2010, 0xE0000002 + 'LLVM Unreachable' on v1.6.2104, 0x80AA001C + 'unknown conversion kind' from v1.6.2106 on -- so match.json is exit-status-only (internal_failure) and a message-matched predicate would have invented a regression at v1.6.2106. The diagnostic half (match-diag.json, POLARITY INVERTED: match = the wanted error is PRESENT) is not independently measurable while the ICE stands -- every release scores invalid-probe and bisect prints 'no release could run this repro', which is the crash, not a flag/profile problem. manual-case-diag-control-matrix.txt closes that gap: on all 21 builds the same invalid base type with a scalar enumerator DOES produce the wanted diagnostic and a valid enum compiles clean. Not an NDEBUG artefact: ErrorHandling.h:101 is '#if 1 // HLSL Change', release builds fail and Compiler Explorer's Linux Release builds SIGSEGV.
summary: Still reproduces on main and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607: "enum EE : uint3 { E = uint3(0,0,0), };" reaches llvm_unreachable("unknown conversion kind") at SemaOverload.cpp:5154 because CheckConvertedConstantConversions does not handle the HLSL-added ICK_* kinds -- measured SCS.Second == ICK_HLSLVector_Truncation. Both halves of the title still hold: it ICEs, and it does not error. The error pow2clk asked for IS already computed ("non-integral type 'uint3' is an invalid underlying type", emitted normally for a scalar-initialised enumerator on all 21 builds) and then discarded when the internal error unwinds. hlsl_clang_trunk already diagnoses it correctly.
title: Integer vector as enum type causes ICE rather than error
